Starting another appliance in the same step does not affect appliances already running. Appliance timing does not depend on insertion order.
Appliances process automatically, so members may leave them. Retrieving a processed item requires a separate interaction. The finished food must be plated using a held dish while facing the appliance containing it.
Each member can hold only one item at a time, and each counter cell can hold only one item. Only one serving must be delivered, with no deadline.

[Map and Coordinates]
The top-left corner is (0,0); x increases to the right and y increases downward.

y=0     X   X   X   P   X
y=1     I   .   X   .   X
y=2     C   .   X   .   X
y=3     D   .   X   .   O

. denotes walkable floor; X denotes an impassable counter where items can be placed or retrieved.
I = ingredient supply; C = chopping board; O = oven; P = pot; B = blender (not used in this recipe); D = dish supply; S = delivery window.
The upper, middle, and lower shared counters are at (2,1), (2,2), and (2,3), respectively, and both members can place and retrieve items there. The upper-left, upper-right, and middle-right private counters are at (1,0), (4,1), and (4,2), respectively.
In this question, items may be placed or retrieved at all 6 reachable counters.
The chef occupies the right corridor and the assistant the left corridor. Neither can pass through counters or appliances.

[Actions and Timing]
In each joint step, both members perform one action. The team clock advances by 1 step; the members' action durations are not added together.
Members may move up, down, left, or right, wait, or interact with the cell directly in front of them. Each move, wait, pickup, placement, start, retrieval, plating, or delivery takes 1 step.
Moving toward a walkable cell changes both position and orientation. Moving toward an impassable cell turns the member toward it without changing position and still takes 1 step.
An interaction requires standing on an adjacent floor cell and facing the target. Within a step, the chef's interaction is resolved first, then the assistant's interaction, followed by movement and appliance processing.
Consequently, an item placed by the assistant in the current step can be picked up by the chef no earlier than the next step.
In a plan, "go to" follows the shortest action path to an adjacent position facing the target. Ties are broken in the order up, down, left, right.
If already in the required position and orientation, navigation takes no time. Wait conditions are checked before each step; if a condition is unsatisfied, the member waits for 1 step. Waiting for processing to finish does not require remaining beside the appliance.

[Permitted Interactions]
Only the correct processing chain for the stated recipe may be executed. Each required ingredient portion may be collected once, and only one serving dish may be collected.
Putting down a held recipe ingredient at an appliance inserts it into that appliance. Processing may start only when all required ingredients are present. Starting an incorrect recipe or adding ingredients to a batch that has started or finished is not allowed.

Items cannot be retrieved during processing. Once an intermediate product is finished, an empty-handed member may retrieve it by name. Only the final food may be plated using a held empty dish; the member continues to hold the plated food.
A member with empty hands may pick up an item from an occupied counter. A member holding an item may put it down on an empty counter.
If the chef places an item first, the assistant may pick it up in the interaction phase of that same step. However, if the assistant's program first specifies "wait until present", the condition must still be checked at the start of the step; this wait cannot be passed early.

Members may move up, down, left, or right, wait, or interact with the cell directly in front of them. Each move, wait, pickup, placement, start, retrieval, plating, or delivery takes 1 step.
Moving toward a walkable cell changes both position and orientation. Moving toward an impassable cell turns the member toward it without changing position and still takes 1 step.
An interaction requires standing on an adjacent floor cell and facing the target. Within a step, the chef's interaction is resolved first, then the assistant's interaction, followed by movement and appliance processing.

If already in the required position and orientation, navigation takes no time. Wait conditions are checked before each step; if a condition is unsatisfied, the member waits for 1 step. Waiting for processing to finish does not require remaining beside the appliance.

[Permitted Interactions]
Only the correct processing chain for the stated recipe may be executed. Each required ingredient portion may be collected once, and only one serving dish may be collected.
Putting down a held recipe ingredient at an appliance inserts it into that appliance. Processing may start only when all required ingredients are present. Starting an incorrect recipe or adding ingredients to a batch that has started or finished is not allowed.
Starting the correct recipe does not require empty hands. A member may start it while holding a dish or another item; starting does not place or consume that held item.
Items cannot be retrieved during processing. Once an intermediate product is finished, an empty-handed member may retrieve it by name. Only the final food may be plated using a held empty dish; the member continues to hold the plated food.
A member with empty hands may pick up an item from an occupied counter. A member holding an item may put it down on an empty counter.
If the chef places an item first, the assistant may pick it up in the interaction phase of that same step. However, if the assistant's program first specifies "wait until present", the condition must still be checked at the start of the step; this wait cannot be passed early.

This question does not permit retrieving ingredients from an appliance that has not started or putting plated final food back on a counter. Once plated, the food must be carried to the delivery window.
Ordinary interaction availability is checked at the start of the step. After the chef interacts, the assistant may also perform a counter pickup or placement whose conditions have just become satisfied. If an assistant interaction that was legal at the start loses its conditions because the chef acts first, it leaves items unchanged but still takes 1 step.

Short-horizon execution still stops at the first attainment of the team goal; in long-horizon execution, unlisted actions are allowed only after both members finish their listed steps.

Both members start simultaneously and execute all their listed steps in order. Each semicolon separates an instruction segment, which may include navigation, a conditional wait, and an interaction, performed in the stated order.
Navigation and waiting may span multiple steps; an interaction takes 1 step. If already at the required position or if a wait condition is already satisfied, proceed directly to the next instruction. Do not insert other tasks between listed steps.
A member who finishes all listed steps first waits. Only after both members finish may subsequent actions be freely arranged, using an optimal continuation for this question's goal.

[Permitted Interactions]

Putting down a held recipe ingredient at an appliance inserts it into that appliance. Processing may start only when all required ingredients are present. Starting an incorrect recipe or adding ingredients to a batch that has started or finished is not allowed.
Starting the correct recipe does not require empty hands. A member may start it while holding a dish or another item; starting does not place or consume that held item.
Items cannot be retrieved during processing. Once an intermediate product is finished, an empty-handed member may retrieve it by name. Only the final food may be plated using a held empty dish; the member continues to hold the plated food.

Items cannot be retrieved during processing. Once an intermediate product is finished, an empty-handed member may retrieve it by name. Only the final food may be plated using a held empty dish; the member continues to hold the plated food.

[Actions and Timing]
In each joint step, both members perform one action. The team clock advances by 1 step; the members' action durations are not added together.
Members may move up, down, left, or right, wait, or interact with the cell directly in front of them. Each move, wait, pickup, placement, start, retrieval, plating, or delivery takes 1 step.
Moving toward a walkable cell changes both position and orientation. Moving toward an impassable cell turns the member toward it without changing position and still takes 1 step.
An interaction requires standing on an adjacent floor cell and facing the target. Within a step, the chef's interaction is resolved first, then the assistant's interaction, followed by movement and appliance processing.
Consequently, an item placed by the assistant in the current step can be picked up by the chef no earlier than the next step.
In a plan, "go to" follows the shortest action path to an adjacent position facing the target. Ties are broken in the order up, down, left, right.
If already in the required position and orientation, navigation takes no time. Wait conditions are checked before each step; if a condition is unsatisfied, the member waits for 1 step. Waiting for processing to finish does not require remaining beside the appliance.

[Permitted Interactions]
Only the correct processing chain for the stated recipe may be executed. Each required ingredient portion may be collected once, and only one serving dish may be collected.
Putting down a held recipe ingredient at an appliance inserts it into that appliance. Processing may start only when all required ingredients are present. Starting an incorrect recipe or adding ingredients to a batch that has started or finished is not allowed.
Starting the correct recipe does not require empty hands. A member may start it while holding a dish or another item; starting does not place or consume that held item.
Items cannot be retrieved during processing. Once an intermediate product is finished, an empty-handed member may retrieve it by name. Only the final food may be plated using a held empty dish; the member continues to hold the plated food.

If the chef places an item first, the assistant may pick it up in the interaction phase of that same step. However, if the assistant's program first specifies "wait until present", the condition must still be checked at the start of the step; this wait cannot be passed early.

Short-horizon execution still stops at the first attainment of the team goal; in long-horizon execution, unlisted actions are allowed only after both members finish their listed steps.

[Plan Execution Protocol]
Both members start simultaneously and execute all their listed steps in order. Each semicolon separates an instruction segment, which may include navigation, a conditional wait, and an interaction, performed in the stated order.
Navigation and waiting may span multiple steps; an interaction takes 1 step. If already at the required position or if a wait condition is already satisfied, proceed directly to the next instruction. Do not insert other tasks between listed steps.
A member who finishes all listed steps first waits. Only after both members finish may subsequent actions be freely arranged, using an optimal continuation for this question's goal.
If the question's goal is reached before the prescribed plan ends, use the time of its first attainment.
A candidate plan may be unable to reach the question's goal. Any such plan is worse than every plan that can reach it. [Actions and Timing]

Members may move up, down, left, or right, wait, or interact with the cell directly in front of them. Each move, wait, pickup, placement, start, retrieval, plating, or delivery takes 1 step.

An explicit "wait in place for N steps" consumes N joint steps while appliances continue processing normally; N is a positive integer. A member with no listed steps waits. Short-horizon execution still stops at the first attainment of the team goal; in long-horizon execution, unlisted actions are allowed only after both members finish their listed steps.

[Plan Execution Protocol]

Options may include advance preparation of resources needed later; these actions also take time. Before reaching the goal, do not insert tasks between listed steps, skip conditional waits, or automatically change handoff locations.

Items cannot be retrieved during processing. Once an intermediate product is finished, an empty-handed member may retrieve it by name. Only the final food may be plated using a held empty dish; the member continues to hold the plated food.

[Permitted Interactions]
Only the correct processing chain for the stated recipe may be executed. Each required ingredient portion may be collected once, and only one serving dish may be collected.
Putting down a held recipe ingredient at an appliance inserts it into that appliance. Processing may start only when all required ingredients are present. Starting an incorrect recipe or adding ingredients to a batch that has started or finished is not allowed.

Items cannot be retrieved during processing. Once an intermediate product is finished, an empty-handed member may retrieve it by name. Only the final food may be plated using a held empty dish; the member continues to hold the plated food.
A member with empty hands may pick up an item from an occupied counter. A member holding an item may put it down on an empty counter.

An explicit "wait in place for N steps" consumes N joint steps while appliances continue processing normally; N is a positive integer. A member with no listed steps waits. Short-horizon execution still stops at the first attainment of the team goal; in long-horizon execution, unlisted actions are allowed only after both members finish their listed steps.

A member who finishes all listed steps first waits. Only after both members finish may subsequent actions be freely arranged, using an optimal continuation for this question's goal.
If the question's goal is reached before the prescribed plan ends, use the time of its first attainment.
A candidate plan may be unable to reach the question's goal. Any such plan is worse than every plan that can reach it. If a wait condition is unmet, waiting must continue; do not skip instructions or automatically change handoff locations. Free continuation is permitted only after both listed programs have finished.

[Actions and Timing]
In each joint step, both members perform one action. The team clock advances by 1 step; the members' action durations are not added together.
Members may move up, down, left, or right, wait, or interact with the cell directly in front of them. Each move, wait, pickup, placement, start, retrieval, plating, or delivery takes 1 step.
Moving toward a walkable cell changes both position and orientation. Moving toward an impassable cell turns the member toward it without changing position and still takes 1 step.
An interaction requires standing on an adjacent floor cell and facing the target. Within a step, the chef's interaction is resolved first, then the assistant's interaction, followed by movement and appliance processing.

In a plan, "go to" follows the shortest action path to an adjacent position facing the target. Ties are broken in the order up, down, left, right.
If already in the required position and orientation, navigation takes no time. Wait conditions are checked before each step; if a condition is unsatisfied, the member waits for 1 step. Waiting for processing to finish does not require remaining beside the appliance.

[Permitted Interactions]
Only the correct processing chain for the stated recipe may be executed. Each required ingredient portion may be collected once, and only one serving dish may be collected.
Putting down a held recipe ingredient at an appliance inserts it into that appliance. Processing may start only when all required ingredients are present. Starting an incorrect recipe or adding ingredients to a batch that has started or finished is not allowed.
Starting the correct recipe does not require empty hands. A member may start it while holding a dish or another item; starting does not place or consume that held item.
Items cannot be retrieved during processing. Once an intermediate product is finished, an empty-handed member may retrieve it by name. Only the final food may be plated using a held empty dish; the member continues to hold the plated food.
A member with empty hands may pick up an item from an occupied counter. A member holding an item may put it down on an empty counter.
If the chef places an item first, the assistant may pick it up in the interaction phase of that same step. However, if the assistant's program first specifies "wait until present", the condition must still be checked at the start of the step; this wait cannot be passed early.
"Wait until an item is present" checks whether that item is at the specified location. An ingredient inserted into an appliance that has not started also counts as present there. A conditional wait does not itself require remaining beside the target.

Ordinary interaction availability is checked at the start of the step. If an assistant interaction that was legal at the start loses its conditions because the chef acts first, it leaves items unchanged but still takes 1 step.

Short-horizon execution still stops at the first attainment of the team goal; in long-horizon execution, unlisted actions are allowed only after both members finish their listed steps.

[Plan Execution Protocol]
Both members start simultaneously and execute all their listed steps in order. Each semicolon separates an instruction segment, which may include navigation, a conditional wait, and an interaction, performed in the stated order.
Navigation and waiting may span multiple steps; an interaction takes 1 step. If already at the required position or if a wait condition is already satisfied, proceed directly to the next instruction. Do not insert other tasks between listed steps.
A member who finishes all listed steps first waits. Only after both members finish may subsequent actions be freely arranged, using an optimal continuation for this question's goal.
If the question's goal is reached before the prescribed plan ends, use the time of its first attainment.
A candidate plan may be unable to reach the question's goal. Any such plan is worse than every plan that can reach it. If a wait condition is unmet, waiting must continue; do not skip instructions or automatically change handoff locations. Free continuation is permitted only after both listed programs have finished.

Members may move up, down, left, or right, wait, or interact with the cell directly in front of them. Each move, wait, pickup, placement, start, retrieval, plating, or delivery takes 1 step.
Moving toward a walkable cell changes both position and orientation. Moving toward an impassable cell turns the member toward it without changing position and still takes 1 step.
An interaction requires standing on an adjacent floor cell and facing the target. Within a step, the chef's interaction is resolved first, then the assistant's interaction, followed by movement and appliance processing.
Consequently, an item placed by the assistant in the current step can be picked up by the chef no earlier than the next step.
In a plan, "go to" follows the shortest action path to an adjacent position facing the target. Ties are broken in the order up, down, left, right.
If already in the required position and orientation, navigation takes no time. Wait conditions are checked before each step; if a condition is unsatisfied, the member waits for 1 step. Waiting for processing to finish does not require remaining beside the appliance.

[Permitted Interactions]
Only the correct processing chain for the stated recipe may be executed. Each required ingredient portion may be collected once, and only one serving dish may be collected.
Putting down a held recipe ingredient at an appliance inserts it into that appliance. Processing may start only when all required ingredients are present. Starting an incorrect recipe or adding ingredients to a batch that has started or finished is not allowed.
Starting the correct recipe does not require empty hands. A member may start it while holding a dish or another item; starting does not place or consume that held item.
Items cannot be retrieved during processing. Once an intermediate product is finished, an empty-handed member may retrieve it by name. Only the final food may be plated using a held empty dish; the member continues to hold the plated food.
A member with empty hands may pick up an item from an occupied counter. A member holding an item may put it down on an empty counter.
If the chef places an item first, the assistant may pick it up in the interaction phase of that same step. However, if the assistant's program first specifies "wait until present", the condition must still be checked at the start of the step; this wait cannot be passed early.
"Wait until an item is present" checks whether that item is at the specified location. An ingredient inserted into an appliance that has not started also counts as present there. A conditional wait does not itself require remaining beside the target.
This question does not permit retrieving ingredients from an appliance that has not started or putting plated final food back on a counter. Once plated, the food must be carried to the delivery window.

After the chef interacts, the assistant may also perform a counter pickup or placement whose conditions have just become satisfied. If an assistant interaction that was legal at the start loses its conditions because the chef acts first, it leaves items unchanged but still takes 1 step.

[Actions and Timing]
In each joint step, both members perform one action. The team clock advances by 1 step; the members' action durations are not added together.
Members may move up, down, left, or right, wait, or interact with the cell directly in front of them. Each move, wait, pickup, placement, start, retrieval, plating, or delivery takes 1 step.
Moving toward a walkable cell changes both position and orientation. Moving toward an impassable cell turns the member toward it without changing position and still takes 1 step.
An interaction requires standing on an adjacent floor cell and facing the target. Within a step, the chef's interaction is resolved first, then the assistant's interaction, followed by movement and appliance processing.
Consequently, an item placed by the assistant in the current step can be picked up by the chef no earlier than the next step.
In a plan, "go to" follows the shortest action path to an adjacent position facing the target. Ties are broken in the order up, down, left, right.
If already in the required position and orientation, navigation takes no time. Wait conditions are checked before each step; if a condition is unsatisfied, the member waits for 1 step. Waiting for processing to finish does not require remaining beside the appliance.

[Permitted Interactions]
Only the correct processing chain for the stated recipe may be executed. Each required ingredient portion may be collected once, and only one serving dish may be collected.
Putting down a held recipe ingredient at an appliance inserts it into that appliance. Processing may start only when all required ingredients are present. Starting an incorrect recipe or adding ingredients to a batch that has started or finished is not allowed.
Starting the correct recipe does not require empty hands. A member may start it while holding a dish or another item; starting does not place or consume that held item.
Items cannot be retrieved during processing. Once an intermediate product is finished, an empty-handed member may retrieve it by name. Only the final food may be plated using a held empty dish; the member continues to hold the plated food.
A member with empty hands may pick up an item from an occupied counter. A member holding an item may put it down on an empty counter.
If the chef places an item first, the assistant may pick it up in the interaction phase of that same step. However, if the assistant's program first specifies "wait until present", the condition must still be checked at the start of the step; this wait cannot be passed early.
"Wait until an item is present" checks whether that item is at the specified location. An ingredient inserted into an appliance that has not started also counts as present there. A conditional wait does not itself require remaining beside the target.
This question does not permit retrieving ingredients from an appliance that has not started or putting plated final food back on a counter. Once plated, the food must be carried to the delivery window.
Ordinary interaction availability is checked at the start of the step. After the chef interacts, the assistant may also perform a counter pickup or placement whose conditions have just become satisfied. If an assistant interaction that was legal at the start loses its conditions because the chef acts first, it leaves items unchanged but still takes 1 step.
Apart from these sequential-resolution cases, do not schedule interactions that are already invalid at the start of a step, such as an empty-handed pickup from an empty counter or placing a held item on an occupied counter.
An explicit "wait in place for N steps" consumes N joint steps while appliances continue processing normally; N is a positive integer. A member with no listed steps waits. Short-horizon execution still stops at the first attainment of the team goal; in long-horizon execution, unlisted actions are allowed only after both members finish their listed steps.

[Plan Execution Protocol]
Both members start simultaneously and execute all their listed steps in order. Each semicolon separates an instruction segment, which may include navigation, a conditional wait, and an interaction, performed in the stated order.
Navigation and waiting may span multiple steps; an interaction takes 1 step. If already at the required position or if a wait condition is already satisfied, proceed directly to the next instruction. Do not insert other tasks between listed steps.
A member who finishes all listed steps first waits. Only after both members finish may subsequent actions be freely arranged, using an optimal continuation for this question's goal.
If the question's goal is reached before the prescribed plan ends, use the time of its first attainment.
A candidate plan may be unable to reach the question's goal. Any such plan is worse than every plan that can reach it. If a wait condition is unmet, waiting must continue; do not skip instructions or automatically change handoff locations. Free continuation is permitted only after both listed programs have finished.

[Permitted Interactions]
Only the correct processing chain for the stated recipe may be executed. Each required ingredient portion may be collected once, and only one serving dish may be collected.
Putting down a held recipe ingredient at an appliance inserts it into that appliance. Processing may start only when all required ingredients are present. Starting an incorrect recipe or adding ingredients to a batch that has started or finished is not allowed.
Starting the correct recipe does not require empty hands. A member may start it while holding a dish or another item; starting does not place or consume that held item.
Items cannot be retrieved during processing. Once an intermediate product is finished, an empty-handed member may retrieve it by name. Only the final food may be plated using a held empty dish; the member continues to hold the plated food.
A member with empty hands may pick up an item from an occupied counter. A member holding an item may put it down on an empty counter.
If the chef places an item first, the assistant may pick it up in the interaction phase of that same step. However, if the assistant's program first specifies "wait until present", the condition must still be checked at the start of the step; this wait cannot be passed early.
"Wait until an item is present" checks whether that item is at the specified location. An ingredient inserted into an appliance that has not started also counts as present there. A conditional wait does not itself require remaining beside the target.
This question does not permit retrieving ingredients from an appliance that has not started or putting plated final food back on a counter. Once plated, the food must be carried to the delivery window.
Ordinary interaction availability is checked at the start of the step. After the chef interacts, the assistant may also perform a counter pickup or placement whose conditions have just become satisfied. If an assistant interaction that was legal at the start loses its conditions because the chef acts first, it leaves items unchanged but still takes 1 step.
Apart from these sequential-resolution cases, do not schedule interactions that are already invalid at the start of a step, such as an empty-handed pickup from an empty counter or placing a held item on an occupied counter.
An explicit "wait in place for N steps" consumes N joint steps while appliances continue processing normally; N is a positive integer. A member with no listed steps waits. Short-horizon execution still stops at the first attainment of the team goal; in long-horizon execution, unlisted actions are allowed only after both members finish their listed steps.

[Plan Execution Protocol]
Both members start simultaneously and execute all their listed steps in order. Each semicolon separates an instruction segment, which may include navigation, a conditional wait, and an interaction, performed in the stated order.
Navigation and waiting may span multiple steps; an interaction takes 1 step. If already at the required position or if a wait condition is already satisfied, proceed directly to the next instruction. Do not insert other tasks between listed steps.
A member who finishes all listed steps first waits. Only after both members finish may subsequent actions be freely arranged, using an optimal continuation for this question's goal.
If the question's goal is reached before the prescribed plan ends, use the time of its first attainment.
A candidate plan may be unable to reach the question's goal. Any such plan is worse than every plan that can reach it. If a wait condition is unmet, waiting must continue; do not skip instructions or automatically change handoff locations. Free continuation is permitted only after both listed programs have finished.

[Permitted Interactions]
Only the correct processing chain for the stated recipe may be executed. Each required ingredient portion may be collected once, and only one serving dish may be collected.
Putting down a held recipe ingredient at an appliance inserts it into that appliance. Processing may start only when all required ingredients are present. Starting an incorrect recipe or adding ingredients to a batch that has started or finished is not allowed.
Starting the correct recipe does not require empty hands. A member may start it while holding a dish or another item; starting does not place or consume that held item.
Items cannot be retrieved during processing. Once an intermediate product is finished, an empty-handed member may retrieve it by name. Only the final food may be plated using a held empty dish; the member continues to hold the plated food.

If the chef places an item first, the assistant may pick it up in the interaction phase of that same step. However, if the assistant's program first specifies "wait until present", the condition must still be checked at the start of the step; this wait cannot be passed early.
"Wait until an item is present" checks whether that item is at the specified location. An ingredient inserted into an appliance that has not started also counts as present there. A conditional wait does not itself require remaining beside the target.
This question does not permit retrieving ingredients from an appliance that has not started or putting plated final food back on a counter. Once plated, the food must be carried to the delivery window.
Ordinary interaction availability is checked at the start of the step. After the chef interacts, the assistant may also perform a counter pickup or placement whose conditions have just become satisfied. If an assistant interaction that was legal at the start loses its conditions because the chef acts first, it leaves items unchanged but still takes 1 step.

Short-horizon execution still stops at the first attainment of the team goal; in long-horizon execution, unlisted actions are allowed only after both members finish their listed steps.

[Plan Execution Protocol]
Both members start simultaneously and execute all their listed steps in order. Each semicolon separates an instruction segment, which may include navigation, a conditional wait, and an interaction, performed in the stated order.
Navigation and waiting may span multiple steps; an interaction takes 1 step. If already at the required position or if a wait condition is already satisfied, proceed directly to the next instruction. Do not insert other tasks between listed steps.
A member who finishes all listed steps first waits. Only after both members finish may subsequent actions be freely arranged, using an optimal continuation for this question's goal.
If the question's goal is reached before the prescribed plan ends, use the time of its first attainment.
A candidate plan may be unable to reach the question's goal. Any such plan is worse than every plan that can reach it. If a wait condition is unmet, waiting must continue; do not skip instructions or automatically change handoff locations. Free continuation is permitted only after both listed programs have finished.

Only the correct processing chain for the stated recipe may be executed. Each required ingredient portion may be collected once, and only one serving dish may be collected.
Putting down a held recipe ingredient at an appliance inserts it into that appliance. Processing may start only when all required ingredients are present. Starting an incorrect recipe or adding ingredients to a batch that has started or finished is not allowed.
Starting the correct recipe does not require empty hands. A member may start it while holding a dish or another item; starting does not place or consume that held item.
Items cannot be retrieved during processing. Once an intermediate product is finished, an empty-handed member may retrieve it by name. Only the final food may be plated using a held empty dish; the member continues to hold the plated food.

If the chef places an item first, the assistant may pick it up in the interaction phase of that same step. However, if the assistant's program first specifies "wait until present", the condition must still be checked at the start of the step; this wait cannot be passed early.

Apart from these sequential-resolution cases, do not schedule interactions that are already invalid at the start of a step, such as an empty-handed pickup from an empty counter or placing a held item on an occupied counter.

Short-horizon execution still stops at the first attainment of the team goal; in long-horizon execution, unlisted actions are allowed only after both members finish their listed steps.

[Actions and Timing]
In each joint step, both members perform one action. The team clock advances by 1 step; the members' action durations are not added together.
Members may move up, down, left, or right, wait, or interact with the cell directly in front of them. Each move, wait, pickup, placement, start, retrieval, plating, or delivery takes 1 step.
Moving toward a walkable cell changes both position and orientation. Moving toward an impassable cell turns the member toward it without changing position and still takes 1 step.
An interaction requires standing on an adjacent floor cell and facing the target. Within a step, the chef's interaction is resolved first, then the assistant's interaction, followed by movement and appliance processing.
Consequently, an item placed by the assistant in the current step can be picked up by the chef no earlier than the next step.
In a plan, "go to" follows the shortest action path to an adjacent position facing the target. Ties are broken in the order up, down, left, right.
If already in the required position and orientation, navigation takes no time. Wait conditions are checked before each step; if a condition is unsatisfied, the member waits for 1 step. Waiting for processing to finish does not require remaining beside the appliance.

[Permitted Interactions]
Only the correct processing chain for the stated recipe may be executed. Each required ingredient portion may be collected once, and only one serving dish may be collected.
Putting down a held recipe ingredient at an appliance inserts it into that appliance. Processing may start only when all required ingredients are present. Starting an incorrect recipe or adding ingredients to a batch that has started or finished is not allowed.
Starting the correct recipe does not require empty hands. A member may start it while holding a dish or another item; starting does not place or consume that held item.
Items cannot be retrieved during processing. Once an intermediate product is finished, an empty-handed member may retrieve it by name. Only the final food may be plated using a held empty dish; the member continues to hold the plated food.
A member with empty hands may pick up an item from an occupied counter. A member holding an item may put it down on an empty counter.
If the chef places an item first, the assistant may pick it up in the interaction phase of that same step. However, if the assistant's program first specifies "wait until present", the condition must still be checked at the start of the step; this wait cannot be passed early.
"Wait until an item is present" checks whether that item is at the specified location. An ingredient inserted into an appliance that has not started also counts as present there. A conditional wait does not itself require remaining beside the target.
This question does not permit retrieving ingredients from an appliance that has not started or putting plated final food back on a counter. Once plated, the food must be carried to the delivery window.
Ordinary interaction availability is checked at the start of the step. After the chef interacts, the assistant may also perform a counter pickup or placement whose conditions have just become satisfied. If an assistant interaction that was legal at the start loses its conditions because the chef acts first, it leaves items unchanged but still takes 1 step.
Apart from these sequential-resolution cases, do not schedule interactions that are already invalid at the start of a step, such as an empty-handed pickup from an empty counter or placing a held item on an occupied counter.
An explicit "wait in place for N steps" consumes N joint steps while appliances continue processing normally; N is a positive integer. A member with no listed steps waits. Short-horizon execution still stops at the first attainment of the team goal; in long-horizon execution, unlisted actions are allowed only after both members finish their listed steps.

[Plan Execution Protocol]
Both members start simultaneously and execute all their listed steps in order. Each semicolon separates an instruction segment, which may include navigation, a conditional wait, and an interaction, performed in the stated order.
Navigation and waiting may span multiple steps; an interaction takes 1 step. If already at the required position or if a wait condition is already satisfied, proceed directly to the next instruction. Do not insert other tasks between listed steps.
A member who finishes all listed steps first waits. Only after both members finish may subsequent actions be freely arranged, using an optimal continuation for this question's goal.
If the question's goal is reached before the prescribed plan ends, use the time of its first attainment.
A candidate plan may be unable to reach the question's goal. Any such plan is worse than every plan that can reach it. If a wait condition is unmet, waiting must continue; do not skip instructions or automatically change handoff locations. Free continuation is permitted only after both listed programs have finished.
